Smt Manju Chandra And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another

High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Mayank Chandra
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Nafees Ahmad, learned counsel for the applicants, Sri Mayank Chandra, learned counsel for the informant and Sri Sunil Kumar, learned A.G.A. for the State as well as perused the record.
3.

The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicants in Case Crime No.07 of 2024, registered under Sections 147, 419, 420, 467, 468, 392, 323, 471, 504, 506 I.P.C. at Police Station- Cantt., District- Prayagraj with a prayer to enlarge them on anticipatory bail.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per prosecution story, the applicant no.1 is the mother and applicant no.2 is the son.
They are stated to have given property belonging to them on rent to the informant for a consideration of Rs.50,000/- per month.

But subsequently, as the said restaurant started running well, the applicants are stated to have gone greedy and asked for share of 50% in the said restaurant or to increase the rent to the tune of Rs.1 lakh per month.

As such, the applicants are stated to have even robbed Rs.45,000/- of the informant and are even stated to have wrongly informed the PDA about the said erection of the restaurant which was demolished, thereby causing loss of Rs.30 lakhs to the informant.
5. Learned counsel for the applicants has stated that they have been falsely implicated in this case.
The FIR is delayed by about more than two months and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
Even the application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. was moved on 28.11.2023, which itself is delayed by about 26 days.
Learned counsel has further stated that applicant no.2 was not present on the alleged date of occurrence as he was under going treatment at Medanta Hospital, Delhi.
It is further stated that no injury has been sustained by any person whatsoever.
There are no criminal antecedents of the applicants.
6. Learned counsel for the applicants has further stated that the case of civil nature pertaining to Rent Control Act has been converted into criminal one by the informant.

It was the informant and his colleagues who were the aggressor party and applicant no.1 had instituted FIR No.241 of 2023 on 4.11.2023 itself against them and the instant FIR is counterblast to the said FIR.
Learned counsel has further stated that subsequent to the said FIR instituted by applicant no.1, two more FIRs have been instituted against the informant and other persons.
7. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicants to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against them.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicants have also been touched upon at length.
The applicants have apprehension of their arrest.

Learned counsel has stated that the applicants undertake that they have co-operated in the investigation and are ready to do so in trial also failing which the State can move appropriate application for cancellation of anticipatory bail.

8. Per contra, learned counsel for the informant and learned A.G.A. have vehemently opposed the anticipatory bail application on the ground that the said land on which the said restaurant has been erected is stated to be a Nazul land as the said information has been provided to the applicants by the District Magistrate, Prayagraj.
Learned counsel has stated that the informant has been enlarged on bail in one case of the three cases mentioned by the counsel for applicants.
It is further stated that the applicants are not entitled for anticipatory bail as they have caused heavy loss to the informant.

9. On due consideration to the arguments advanced by learned counsels for the parties and taking into consideration the delay in lodging the FIR and there being an FIR instituted by applicant no.1 against the informant and other persons, the applicants are liable to be enlarged on anticipatory bail in view of the judgment of Supreme Court in the case of "Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi),
(2020) 5 SCC 1".
